{"number": 4187, "title": "fix(OMN-19810): the wrapper's PATH-shadow warning resolves a symlink before warning", "draft": false, "labels": [], "head": {"ref": "jonah/omn-19810-wrapper-shadow-warning-resolves-symlink", "sha": "dbc163c636b76fc707bb55d8892c5ba09108e216"}, "mergeable": true, "mergeable_state": "blocked", "state": "closed", "merged": false, "merged_at": null, "body": "Cites OMN-19810. Companion to #4185, which fixes the same defect in `scripts/reconcile-host.sh`; this PR fixes it in the wrapper `scripts/onex`. The two PRs touch disjoint files and land in either order.

## Problem

`_warn_on_shadowed_path_onex` compares `command -v onex` against `$SCRIPT_DIR/onex` as raw strings. `command -v` returns a symlink's own path, unresolved, so a `~/.local/bin/onex` symlink whose target is this wrapper (the sanctioned way to put `onex` on PATH, present on the operator Mac since 2026-09-26T15:37Z) prints the "a different 'onex' shadows the CLI venv" warning on every dispatch. Lanes chasing today's delegate refusals read that warning as the cause, and it is not a shadow.

## Fix

When the PATH `onex` is a symlink, resolve it with a portable loop (the same relative-link handling the wrapper already uses for its own location, plus `pwd -P` on the directory) and skip the warning when it lands on this wrapper or on the dispatch entrypoint. A symlink to anything else, and a regular file, still warn. The common case, no symlink, starts no extra process.

## Tests

`tests/scripts/test_onex_wrapper.py`, 3 new cases:
- `test_no_warning_when_path_onex_is_a_symlink_to_this_wrapper` (red before the fix)
- `test_no_warning_when_a_relative_symlink_chain_reaches_this_wrapper` (red before the fix)
- `test_warning_still_fires_for_a_symlink_to_anything_else` (the negative case)

`uv run pytest tests/scripts/test_onex_wrapper.py tests/scripts/test_onex_wrapper_floor_omn17309.py -q`: 62 passed. `shellcheck -S warning scripts/onex`: clean. `pre-commit run --files` on both files: exit 0.

## Lab line: host readback (operator Mac, 2026-09-26T20:2xZ)

The wrapper is a host script, not runtime code, so there is no .201 dev-lane (lab) surface for it; the readback is on the host where the symlink lives, counting warning lines on `--version`:
- new wrapper, PATH `onex` a symlink to it: 0
- new wrapper, PATH `onex` the existing `~/.local/bin/onex` (a symlink to a different copy, the canonical clone): 1 (control, still warns)
- current canonical wrapper, PATH `onex` the existing `~/.local/bin/onex` symlink to itself: 1 (the defect)

## Not in this PR

The delegate refusals themselves (exit 3, below the proven floor) come from the reconcile never restamping the floor while `onex-path-shadow` fails; #4185 is that fix. After #4185 lands on `dev` and the canonical clone fast-forwards, the next reconcile restamps the floor and `onex delegate` runs again.

Evidence-Ticket: OMN-19810
Evidence-Source: OCC#11526
"}

{"number": 4190, "title": "feat(OMN-19812): C28 producer -- consumer-flow observability re-measured on the dev lane, not read once by hand", "draft": false, "labels": [], "head": {"ref": "jonah/omn-19812-c28-consumer-flow-probe", "sha": "4afd863b2bf335d731afe2d2daa5e4847d06fe0f"}, "mergeable": true, "mergeable_state": "blocked", "state": "open", "merged": false, "merged_at": null, "body": "## OMN-19812: C28 producer

Beta criterion C28 (consumer-flow observability on the runtime) rested on one hand READBACK, taken on the `.201` dev lane at 2026-09-19T12:20Z. No workflow re-took it. An image that stopped registering a flow counter for one subscription kind, a projection-api that stopped paging, or a stall-alert seam that went back to discarding payloads would have left C28 reading GREEN on the board indefinitely. This is the condition the C12 producer fixed, on another criterion.

This PR adds the producer. Its exit code is C28's verdict, the same shape as C11, C12 and C15. The board registration is OmniNode-ai/omninode_infra#1713, which should merge after this PR, which moves the READBACK prose to EVIDENCE.

### What it measures: the readback's own clauses

| clause | what is graded (31 checks) |
| --- | --- |
| kinds (clause 1) | The consumer-flow exposure is walked in full 4 times, 30 s apart. Both kinds the proof sentence names must have a row in every sample: the audit-purpose projection consumer (`node_gateway_link_health_projection_compute`, `consumer_purpose: audit`) and the publishing reducer (`projection_consumer_flow`). Each row needs integer counters and a state other than UNKNOWN. The window must advance across samples, and the kind's counter must move: `messages_in` for the audit consumer and `messages_out` for the reducer, which is the half of the flow-counter registration fix that is about reducer publishes being attributed. Groups are matched up to `consume.` so a contract version bump does not read as a missing kind. |
| negative (clause 2) | The two flow-counter registration test files pass on the checkout. With `flow_counters.register(...)` removed from `_make_event_bus_callback`, only the `[event_bus]` cases and the AST gate fail. With it removed from `_make_raw_event_projection_callback`, only the `[raw_event_projection]` cases and the AST gate fail. The other branch's cases must still pass under each mutation, which shows the module imported and ran. After each run the source is restored byte for byte and checked by sha256. |
| cursor (clause 3) | The live 10-minute window is read first, from `omnidash_analytics.omninode_internal.consumer_flow_windows`. Then the exposure is walked with its declared `since` cursor until `next_cursor` is null. The walk must terminate, a page at `row_limit` must carry a cursor, and no live group may be unreachable. The readback's negative control, where the undeclared `?cursor=` returns page 1 again, is taken again and recorded. |
| boot (premise) | The applied topic must advance on its own before the probe publishes anything. The runtime logs for this boot must show zero stall-alert validation errors, counting both model names the seam has had (`...Request` and `...Trigger`). The zero is then proven live: one malformed trigger is published with its envelope copied from the newest real message, and the seam must raise a validation error, log `boundary_swallow_prevented dlq_routed=true` with the injected correlation id, and put the marker on the generic DLQ. |

Exit codes: 0 means every check held, 1 means at least one failed and the record names it, 2 means the probe could not look. Could-not-look covers a lane container that is not healthy, a boot that changed under the run twice, and docker, the broker, the database or the exposure refusing. A record is written in every case.

**The one write** is that malformed payload, which is exactly what the readback did. Its correlation id carries the fixed prefix `c28c28c2-c28c-`, so a later run on the same boot can exclude its own errors. An error with no paired boundary line is never excused. The broker credential is read by `rpk` inside the broker container and never reaches the job. No repository secret is used.

**Recorded, not graded:** the per-seam DLQ high-watermark and the DLQ copy count. These are the two findings the readback recorded on the stall-alert payload ticket. Grading them would add a criterion, not re-measure this one.

### Files

- `.github/workflows/chain-canary-c28-consumer-flow.yml`: runs 4x/day at `:13` (0,6,12,18) plus `workflow_dispatch`, on `[self-hosted, omnibase-verify, host-201]`. It has no pull_request trigger, for the same reason the C11 header gives.
- `scripts/ci/c28_consumer_flow_probe.py`: the grader and collector, standard library only.
- `tests/ci/test_c28_consumer_flow_probe.py`: 37 offline tests. 21 of them break one property each and assert FAIL names the check. Three use real bytes captured from the dev lane: the seam's log lines for a probe-prefixed injection, the same lines for a hand injection with an ordinary correlation id (which must count as natural), and `rpk topic describe -p` output. The mutation is exercised against the real `handler_wiring.py`.
- Registered in `config/ci_evidence_policy.yaml` (+ `EXPECTED_EVIDENCE_IDS`), `config/lab_probe_windows.yaml`, `NEW_VERIFY_JOBS` in `tests/ci/test_verify_runner_runs_on_omn18408.py`, a pre-commit grader hook, and the replay `debt_baseline`, which uses the same wording as the C11, C12 and C16 probe entries.

### Lab-first: runs on the host-201 verify runner against the `.201` dev lane

Host `.201`, lane dev (compose project `omnibase-infra`), runner `omnibase-verify` on `host-201`. The command is this workflow, run on the branch: https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/omnibase_infra/actions/runs/36268917975 at head `4afd863b`, which is this PR's head.

- **Attempt 2, 2026-09-26T21:25Z, on the dev-lane boot of 21:19Z (the deploy agent's own redeploy): GREEN, all 31 checks, exit 0.** Clause 1: the audit consumer `...gateway_link_health_projection_compute.consume.1.0.0` read in=2 out=0, the publishing reducer `...projection_consumer_flow.consume.1.0.1` read in=4 out=565, and the window advanced across 4 samples. Clause 2: 11 passed clean, and each branch mutation gave 3 failed / 8 passed, with only that branch's cases and the AST gate failing. Clause 3: 409 live groups in the table and all 409 reached by a two-page walk (500 rows with a cursor, then 61 with none). `?cursor=` returned page 1 again. Boot: the applied topic advanced from 272459 to 272471 over 90 s, with zero natural validation errors across 21,391 and 4,591 log lines. The injected trigger was refused (2 error lines), dead-lettered under its own `c28c28c2-c28c-` correlation id, and present on the generic DLQ. The per-seam DLQ still reads 0, which is recorded.
- **Attempt 1, around 20:15Z, on the 19:32Z boot: RED, 1 of 31.** `zero_natural_stall_alert_validation_errors` counted 12 natural lines. They were my own positive-control publish, made by hand at 19:34Z with an ordinary correlation id while I was working out the seam's log shape. The probe cannot tell that from a real error and does not excuse it. That red is the gate working on the real lane. The other 30 checks passed on the runner.
- Before the workflow existed, the lane half of the script was also hand-run on the host with `python3` (19:41Z): 21 of 22 lane checks passed, and the one red was the same hand publish.

**About the branch-scoped `push:` trigger in this head.** `workflow_dispatch` cannot reach a workflow that is not yet on the default branch (the API answers 404), so a `push:` trigger scoped to this branch name is what let the branch run on the lab runner. After merge it fires on nothing, because the branch is deleted. The commit that removes it was refused by the always-run `consumer-kwarg-parity` pre-commit hook. That hook broke on dev independently of this PR: omnimarket#2841 (merged 21:10Z) now splats `**kwargs` into `dispatch()` and declares `no_escalation`, which `ProtocolDelegationDispatchPort` here does not accept. This PR does not touch that seam. The trigger will be removed once that drift is fixed.

### Local verification

- `uv run --frozen pytest tests/ci/test_c28_consumer_flow_probe.py tests/ci/test_ci_evidence_policy.py tests/ci/test_verify_runner_runs_on_omn18408.py tests/ci/test_check_lab_probe_windows.py -q`: all pass.
- Positive control on the grader tests: removing the unreachable-group condition from the grader makes `test_red_when_a_live_group_is_unreachable` fail.
- `check_lab_probe_windows.py` across omnibase_infra, omninode_infra and omnimarket: OK, 12 entries. `check_incident_replay_coverage.py`: OK.
- `ruff format` / `ruff check` / `mypy --strict` on the new script and test: clean. The pre-commit hooks ran on commit, with no bypass.

Evidence-Ticket: OMN-19812
Evidence-Source: OCC#11537
"}

{"number": 4193, "title": "fix(OMN-18812): re-run a preflight whose companion merged, in omnibase_infra", "draft": false, "labels": [], "head": {"ref": "jonah/omn-18812-companion-merge-heal-omnibase-infra", "sha": "a779b8042d921822c2d4306256fdffca1486face"}, "mergeable": true, "mergeable_state": "blocked", "state": "open", "merged": false, "merged_at": null, "body": "## OMN-18812 follow-up 2: the companion-merge heal, ported to omnibase_infra

**Merge order: this PR is stacked on omnibase_infra#4192 and lands after it.** Its branch carries the single commit of #4192 (946239e98), because this repo's always-run pre-commit hook `onex-delegation-dispatch-consumer-kwarg-parity` is red on plain `dev` against current omnimarket, and #4192 is the fix for that. Once #4192 squash-merges, those two files are already on `dev` with identical content, so the change in this PR is the last commit only (a779b8042).

**Problem.** `occ-preflight / eligibility` waits 1500 s for the cited change-control companion and then fails closed. When the companion merges later, nothing in this repo re-runs the preflight. The existing `occ-preflight-heal` here listens to `pull_request: edited` and `workflow_run: completed`, and both of those fire before the median companion merges. So the PR stays red until a person or a drain lane types `gh run rerun --failed`. omniclaude fixed this on 2026-09-19 with a scheduled heal (omniclaude#2270, #2272). That heal exists only in omniclaude.

**What this adds.**

- The same heal, copied: `.github/workflows/occ-companion-merge-heal.yml`, `scripts/ci/occ_companion_merge_heal.py` and `tests/ci/test_occ_companion_merge_heal_omn18812.py`. The logic is unchanged from omniclaude at d9cfb4c6f. The only differences are a provenance paragraph in the workflow header, `setup-python` pinned to a commit SHA, two `noqa` comments that the ruff config here reports as unused, and one compound test assertion split in two.
- **The incident replay that the incident-replay coverage gate here requires for a new guard:** `tests/ci/test_incident_replay_omn18812.py`, over `tests/fixtures/omn18812/`, registered in `tests/incident_replays/registry.yaml`.
  - The fixtures are verbatim `gh api` reads of a real stale red, compressed with `gzip -n -9`. The bytes are already public on the PRs they come from.
  - The incident is omnibase_infra#3999. Its preflight and OCC Companion Merged Gate failed at 18:02–18:46Z on 2026-09-23, its companion OCC#10983 merged at 20:35:00Z, and it was still red when captured three days later.
  - The replay drives the real guard. The guard must select exactly the three runs whose own preflight-family job failed (35898373010, 35898372640, 35898371776) and leave alone the three runs that failed for other reasons.
  - The discriminator is omnibase_infra#4191, whose companion OCC#11538 was open at capture. The guard must refuse it without reading a single run.
  - Both directions are mutation-proved. Removing the merged-companion precondition turns the discriminator red, and matching every failed job instead of only the preflight family turns the incident case red.

**No gate is weakened.** The re-run executes the same validators against the merged companion and can still fail. A PR still cannot merge before its companion does. The heal is not a required check. It uses only the ambient `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`actions: write` on its one job), so no new credential is added.

## Proof

- **Replay against real PRs (read-only dry run of this exact script, 2026-09-26T21:50Z, `--repo OmniNode-ai/omnibase_infra --dry-run`).** It would re-run #3999 (3 runs) and #2658 (5 runs, companion OCC#6083 merged). It refused the 9 PRs whose companion is still open and the 4 whose body has no stamp.
- **The write path is proven live in omniclaude.** Heal run 36230786411 re-ran the failed jobs of 20 runs at 2026-09-26T08:47Z.
- **Local:** 89 tests pass (the heal suite plus the replay), and `mypy --strict` is clean. Pre-commit passed on the commit, including the `incident-replay-coverage` hook.
- **Lab:** not runtime-affecting. The change is a CI workflow, a CI script and tests, with no runtime or image impact.

## Expected effect

The merge-throughput measurement for 2026-09-26 found 140 of 221 product merges bound to a companion. They averaged 2.44h from push to merge, against 0.92h for PRs without one: 212 extra PR-hours in one day. This heal caps the wait after a companion merges at the 10-minute schedule plus the re-run time.

Evidence-Ticket: OMN-18812
Evidence-Source: OCC#11543

"}

{"number": 2857, "title": "feat(OMN-19407): the onex CLI reads task classes from the authority through the onex.contracts registry", "draft": false, "labels": [], "head": {"ref": "jonah/omn-19407-onex-cli-registry-vocabulary", "sha": "f77b51f26e671bf8b41661a8a7e5514b5ae975cb"}, "mergeable": false, "mergeable_state": "dirty", "state": "open", "merged": false, "merged_at": null, "body": "## Summary

Operator ruling 2026-09-24: the `onex` CLI keeps no list of its own; everything it offers, validates or classifies against is read from the registry. This PR makes the task-class authority the thing the CLI reads, and removes the hand-written copies in this repo's own CLI surfaces.

- **New entry-point group `onex.contracts`.** `task_class_authority = omnimarket.inference.task_class_authority:load_task_class_authority`. A consumer (the `onex delegate` CLI in omnibase_infra) resolves the task-class contract through this entry at run time, with no package path and no import of omnimarket.
- **The authority answers every question the CLI used to answer from mirror models.** `ModelTaskClassAuthority` gains `resolve_task_type(prompt, explicit=)` (word-boundary, presence-only selection gated by shape, deterministic tie-break, declared fallback), `execution_budget(task_class)`, `unroutable_task_classes` and `unroutable_refusal()`. An explicit internal class is admitted by name; a class carrying `routing_availability` is refused in the contract's words; an unknown class is refused naming every declared class.
- **The fallback is the contract's.** `task_class_contracts.v1.yaml` declares `selection_fallback: document` with its rationale; the loader refuses a fallback that is not public. It was a constant inside the CLI before.
- **`routing_availability`** is typed (`ModelRoutingAvailability`, `EnumRoutingAvailabilityStatus`) on each entry.
- The 240-second execution-ceiling bound moved onto `ModelTaskClassExecutionBudget` (it lived on the CLI's mirror model).
- **`onex cloud delegate --task-type`** reads the authority's public classes through `ChoiceFromAuthority` when the command runs; `CLOUD_TASK_TYPE_CHOICES` is deleted.
- **`onex-delegate` adapter and the orchestrator `__main__`** read `task_type`, `source` and the quality-contract mode from the wire request model's declared fields; `_ALLOWED_TASK_TYPES`, `_ALLOWED_SOURCES` (which lacked `external-client`) and the copied mode choices are deleted.

## Tests

- New `tests/unit/inference/test_task_class_resolution_omn19407.py`: resolution, explicit internal admission, unroutable refusal, fallback declaration and its validation, budget lookup, and the fallback's floor properties (shape-agnostic blocking floors, a positive control on `research` and `planning`, `identifiers_grounded` armed) against the live contract. These properties moved here from the CLI's committed floors extract, which the companion infra PR deletes.
- New `tests/unit/cli/test_cli_cloud_registry_vocabulary.py`: `onex cloud delegate` offers exactly what the authority declares, read per invocation.
- Pinned copies removed from `test_task_class_authority_omn15651.py`, `test_task_class_selection_omn18305.py`, `test_task_class_selection_omn18831.py` and the orchestrator `test_contract.py`.
- Focused run: 136 passed. `ruff format`, `ruff check`, `mypy --strict` on the changed modules: clean. Pre-commit hooks passed on every commit.

## Ordering

This PR must be merged **and released into the dispatch venv before** the companion omnibase_infra PR (same ticket), because that CLI refuses by name when `onex.contracts:task_class_authority` is not advertised, and it is not advertised by any released omnimarket yet. That refusal was checked against the current dispatch venv: `onex delegate --help` exits 2 with "no installed distribution advertises 'task_class_authority' in the 'onex.contracts' entry-point group".

`task_class_contracts.v1.yaml` is also edited by omnimarket#2854 and #2852. The edit here is one new top-level `selection_fallback` block after `execution_budgets`, so it rebases cleanly on either.

## Proof (pre-PR, branch build)

This branch plus the infra branch, installed editable into a copy of the dispatch venv on the Mac (Homebrew 3.13), run against the `.201` dev lane with `--bus kafka --lane dev`. The drift override was set because this is a branch build, so these runs are proof of the branch and are not evidence receipts.

- `onex delegate --help` lists exactly the contract's 15 classes: public (11), internal by explicit name only (`documentation`, `escalation`, `validator_generation`), not routable (`agent_delegation`), and fallback `document`.
- `--task-type documentation`: success on Qwen3.8-27B, quality gate passed, score 1.0 (run fd649fae).
- `--task-type validator_generation`: resolved and dispatched; the orchestrator then refused it with "required_bar missing for task_class 'validator_generation'" (run be1bffe3).
- `--task-type escalation`: resolved and dispatched on gemini-2.5-flash; the grade failed with "no deterministic acceptance or judge adequacy authority" (run 46732b29).
- `--task-type agent_delegation`: refused before dispatch, quoting the contract's `pending_capability` block.

Resolution works for every class. The validator_generation and escalation failures happen after resolution, in the quality-bar policy that omnimarket#2854 changes.

{"number": 2900, "title": "fix(OMN-18143): the deploy effect publishes the rebuild command and returns, so a real deploy no longer runs into the 600 s dispatch deadline", "draft": false, "labels": [{"name": "hold:auto-merge"}], "head": {"ref": "jonah/omn-18143-deploy-effect-publishes-and-returns", "sha": "8ae5128d302523e2925a7fef7cd03e9a41a5b026"}, "mergeable": true, "mergeable_state": "unstable", "state": "open", "merged": false, "merged_at": null, "body": "## What

`node_redeploy_deploy_effect` no longer waits for the deploy agent's answer. The command arm publishes the rebuild command, records it, and returns. The outcome is decided by the durable `rebuild-completed` arm, when the agent's completion arrives.

Ticket: OMN-18143, AC3: "Awaiting a completion event does not block the intake of later commands for the same lane."

**Stacked on #2897, which is stacked on #2896. Land them in this order: #2896, then #2897, then this PR.** The base branch is #2897's branch, so this diff shows only this change.

## Why

- A real rebuild takes about 20 minutes. The command arm waited up to 600 s for the answer, and the runtime abandons any dispatch after 600 s (`consumer_dispatch_deadline_seconds`, OMN-19355).
- So the first dispatch of every real deploy command went to `onex.dlq.omnibase-infra.intents.v1` as `dispatch_deadline_exceeded`. `node_dlq_replay_effect` then replayed it about every 10 minutes. In the window 2026-09-24T19:00Z to 2026-09-25T06:37Z, 22 of the 50 extra rebuild-requested publishes followed such a replay (OMN-19377 comment, 2026-09-25T07:39:37Z).
- #2897 makes those replays harmless. The quarantine itself still happened on every deploy: a false failure in the DLQ that the handler-errors alert (#2879) reports.
- Each abandoned dispatch also counts toward the bus's orphan limit. At 3 orphans the bus reports UNHEALTHY (`consumer_dispatch_orphan_limit`, omnibase_infra `event_bus_kafka.py` `_adopt_orphaned_dispatch`).
- The serial consumer held every later deploy-publish command behind the wait.
- The correlation-scoped monitor subscription also left one `redeploy-deploy-effect-<corr8>` consumer group behind per deploy. 120 of them were live on 2026-09-16 (OMN-17888). That subscription is removed.

## How

- **Command arm.** It checks the grant and runs #2897's publish-once check, both unchanged. It then **stages** the command under `ONEX_STATE_DIR`, publishes it, records it and returns, with metric `rebuild_published`. It opens no subscription.
  - The record now also carries `rollback_target` and `smoke_test`.
  - A staged command does not count as published, so a publish that raised is still published on redelivery. #2897's AC4 is kept.
- **Completion arm.** `DeployPublishRecord.settle` returns the staged or recorded entry once and marks it settled, inside one locked read-modify-write.
  - The rollback reason is computed from the completion and the recorded smoke flag. The rolled-back fact is emitted as a handler-output event, with the recorded rollback target.
  - A redelivered completion finds the entry already settled and emits nothing. The orchestrator terminalises every rolled-back fact it receives.
  - A settled entry stays published, so a replay of the same command is still skipped.
  - If a completion arrives before the record write, it settles the staged entry. The record write keeps the settled mark.
- **Rejection arm.** It is the only place that sees a `busy` now, and it releases the record there (#2897's semantics).
- **Timeout rollback removed.** It rolled back a healthy 20-minute rebuild from a dispatch the runtime had already abandoned. The lab convergence guard (OMN-18144) is the place to report silence from the agent.
- **Contract.** `timeout_ms` is now 30000 (it was 660000, sized for the wait). The descriptions are updated. Topics and routing are unchanged.
- **Constructor.** `timeout_s` and `poll_interval_s` are removed from `HandlerDeployPublishMonitor`. `publish_and_monitor` is replaced by `publish_rebuild_command`, which returns `None`.

- **RED first**, commit 7a43efa06: 5 failed, 1 passed. `tests/test_omn18143_deploy_effect_publishes_and_returns.py` failed because the dispatch still blocked past a 5 s budget with the production 600 s timeout.
  - The first draft of this test came from `onex delegate --task-type test`, run 73006e87. Its logic was right. One import path was wrong (`omnimarket.testing.orchestrator_handler`), so it failed as-is and was edited.
- **GREEN**, commit 8ae5128d3: 178 passed over the 16 focused files that touch this node (local run). `mypy --strict` passes on the node. `ruff` is clean. The commit hooks ran and passed.
- **Negative controls** (local):

{"number": 2955, "title": "feat(OMN-19513): the emit registry routes hook.event and redaction governs nested members by dotted name", "draft": false, "labels": [], "head": {"ref": "jonah/omn-19513-hook-event-registration", "sha": "0e762b2dd06d6cbef0e6246093770f660694a02d"}, "mergeable": false, "mergeable_state": "dirty", "state": "open", "merged": false, "merged_at": null, "body": "Ticket: OMN-19513. ## Why
Operator ruling requires capturing all hooks. The omniclaude producer journals one `hook.event` per Claude Code hook call.

Local after the merges: ruff format and check clean, mypy --strict clean on redaction.py, 159 focused tests passed (node_event_emit_effect capture, redaction and enrichment tests plus node_emit_daemon), pre-commit clean on the PR's own files. Checked outside CI: omniclaude#2371's registry-consistency checker passes against this branch's topics.yaml and fails against dev's.

### Implementation Details
The capture redaction contract gains a policy for the new topic. Every member of nested `lineage` and `payload` objects is declared by dotted name as `capture_verbatim`. The tool-executed topic policy gains `tool_use_id` and `agent_id` as `capture_verbatim`. The topic is not added to either node's `publish_topics` list because the consumer is built by a separate lane and the contract graph gate refuses producers without consumers. {"number": 2964, "title": "fix(OMN-19765): a BYOK-substituted attempt names the backend it replaced", "draft": false, "labels": [], "head": {"ref": "jonah/omn-19765-pin-honours-byok-substitution", "sha": "0138bd68e26605bb64593df522d5b564cdd6c6a7"}, "mergeable": true, "mergeable_state": "blocked", "state": "open", "merged": false, "merged_at": null, "body": "## What changes
- `ModelResolvedDelegationBackend` gains an optional `substituted_from_backend_id` field.
- `substitute_local_byok_route` sets it to the pinned/house backend id (e.g. `cloud-glm`) it replaced when it substitutes a customer's BYOK rung (e.g. `byok-glm`); unchanged (no substitution) paths leave it `None`.
- `ModelDelegateSkillAttemptRecord` (wire model) declares the same field; `LocalDelegationDispatchPort`'s three attempt-record sites in `port_local_delegation_dispatch.py` now thread `backend.substituted_from_backend_id` through.
- `handler_delegate_skill.py`'s `_attempt_records` reads it off the raw dict for the local-dispatch-port carrier shape.

## Why
On a machine with a locally registered BYOK key, `substitute_local_byok_route` replaces a HOUSE rung (e.g. the platform `cloud-glm` backend) with the customer's own declared BYOK rung (`byok-glm`) before dispatch. The resolved backend carried no memory of what it replaced, so a caller who pinned `cloud-glm` had no way to distinguish "answered on the SAME backend I pinned, via my own key" from "escalated to something else entirely" -- both looked identical: an accepted attempt naming a `backend_id` other than the pin.

Found by a peer lane working the parent delegation-routing epic: run `86538bdd-0a35-47c6-98e1-b4d13ad39e55` answered on the first attempt by `glm-5.3-flash` via the BYOK route, yet the `omnibase_infra` CLI's pin check reported a false escalation because it had only the raw `backend_id` strings to compare.

## Testing
Host `Stickybeatz-Studio.local`, lane `glm-pin-exit-fix-83`. No lab surface is involved: this is a pure library change exercised with focused unit tests and, via the companion PR's proof, a real in-process delegation run on the local Mac -- not a runtime-affecting change to a deployed lane.

- New RED-first test: `tests/unit/delegation/test_omn19765_byok_substitution_attribution.py` -- a pinned `cloud-glm` run with a registered `glm` key now names `cloud-glm` as the substituted backend; an unsubstituted or keyless rung stays `None`. Confirmed RED against the pre-fix code (reverted `local_byok_route.py`'s new line locally, reran, restored) before implementing.
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/delegation/ -m "not kafka"`: 1799 passed, 2 skipped.
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/nodes/node_delegate_skill_orchestrator tests/integration/node_delegate_skill_orchestrator -m "not kafka"`: 299 passed, 4 skipped.
- `uv run ruff format --check` / `uv run ruff check` on changed files: clean.
- `uv run mypy --strict` on changed files: clean.
- `pre-commit` (file-scoped; `mypy-type-check` skipped in the manual local run since it is a directory-wide hook -- it ran clean at push time via the governed pre-push leg) and the governed pre-push hook: clean.

## Landing order
Land this PR before the companion `omnibase_infra` PR ("the pin check honours a local BYOK-substituted attempt", same ticket's AC2/AC3). This PR is additive and backward-compatible on its own (a new optional field, default `None`); the infra PR reads the field but degrades safely (treats it as absent) if landed first, so the order is a preference for a clean history rather than a hard dependency.

## Related
Companion `omnibase_infra` PR reads this field to honour the pin at the CLI's `_backend_pin_defect` check. No file overlap with the open PR that touches the deployed-lane dogfood fault-pin guard for this ticket's parent (that PR touches the runtime dogfood fault-route files; the companion PR here touches only the CLI's pin check and its read-side attempt mirror).

Evidence-Ticket: OMN-19765
Evidence-Source: OCC#11498
"}

{"number": 2973, "title": "fix(OMN-18812): re-run a preflight whose companion merged, in omnimarket", "draft": false, "labels": [], "head": {"ref": "jonah/omn-18812-companion-merge-heal-omnimarket", "sha": "ad1421665e4930932e68dee8acfe44e9939b01a3"}, "mergeable": true, "mergeable_state": "blocked", "state": "open", "merged": false, "merged_at": null, "body": "## OMN-18812 follow-up 2: the companion-merge heal, ported to omnimarket

**Problem.** `occ-preflight / eligibility` waits 1500 s for the cited change-control companion and then fails closed. When the companion merges later, nothing in this repo re-runs the preflight, so the PR stays red until a person or a drain lane types `gh run rerun --failed`. omniclaude fixed this on 2026-09-19 with a scheduled heal (omniclaude#2270, #2272). That heal exists only in omniclaude.

**What this adds.** The same heal, copied: `.github/workflows/occ-companion-merge-heal.yml`, `scripts/ci/occ_companion_merge_heal.py` and `tests/ci/test_occ_companion_merge_heal_omn18812.py`. Every 10 minutes it reads each open PR. If the PR has a failed preflight check and its cited change-control companion has MERGED, it re-runs the failed jobs of only those runs whose own preflight-family job failed. The logic is unchanged from omniclaude at d9cfb4c6f. The only differences are a provenance paragraph in the workflow header, `setup-python` pinned to a commit SHA (the action pin ratchet here), and one compound test assertion split in two.

**No gate is weakened.** The re-run executes the same validators against the merged companion and can still fail. A PR still cannot merge before its companion does. The heal is not a required check. It uses only the ambient `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`actions: write` on its one job), so no new credential is added.

## Proof

- **Replay against real PRs (read-only dry run of this exact script, 2026-09-26T21:50Z, `--repo OmniNode-ai/omnimarket --dry-run`).** It found 6 open PRs whose companion had merged while the preflight stayed red: #2960 (OCC#11479, merged 20:30Z), #2939 and #2938 (OCC#11437, merged 10:41Z), #2913 (OCC#11315), #2905 (OCC#11275) and #2886 (OCC#11472, merged 17:36Z). That is 34 failed runs the heal would re-run. It refused the 10 PRs whose companion is still open and the 7 whose body has no stamp.
- **The write path is proven live in omniclaude.** Heal run 36230786411 re-ran the failed jobs of 20 runs at 2026-09-26T08:47Z.
- **Local:** the test file passes (83 tests), `mypy --strict` is clean on the script, and pre-commit passes on the changed files.
- **Lab:** not runtime-affecting. The change is a CI workflow and a CI script, with no runtime or image impact.

## Expected effect

The merge-throughput measurement for 2026-09-26 found 140 of 221 product merges bound to a companion. They averaged 2.44h from push to merge, against 0.92h for PRs without one: 212 extra PR-hours in one day. In 55 of them the product PR still waited after its companion merged (p50 0.41h, p90 2.72h). This heal caps that wait at the 10-minute schedule plus the re-run time.

Evidence for the write path in this repo: after merge, the first scheduled run whose log shows `re-ran failed jobs of run …`.

Evidence-Ticket: OMN-18812
Evidence-Source: OCC#11541

{"number": 441, "title": "fix(OMN-19762): a failed provider-key save says which failure, and a timeout stops asking for a retry", "draft": false, "labels": [], "head": {"ref": "jake/omn-19762-credential-failure-copy", "sha": "2b17738bd0f7ad7091eac65547b267c664f0e18e"}, "mergeable": null, "mergeable_state": "unknown", "state": "closed", "merged": true, "merged_at": "2026-09-26T15:29:07Z", "body": "## What this fixes

`app/(app)/app/inference-credentials/actions.ts` read the upstream status, wrote it to `console.error`, and then discarded it in favour of one sentence — **"Failed to save credential. Please try again."** — that covered a timeout, an unreachable service and a rejection alike.

Two consequences, both observed on onex-dev:

1. **A customer whose save timed out was told to try again.** The 504 is this client's *own* abort — `lib/api-client.ts:37` aborts every onex-api call at `ONEX_API_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 8000) and `:218` maps the `AbortError` to `ApiError(504)`. Aborting the caller's wait does not cancel the server's write: `onex-api` recorded `201 Created` for a save whose caller had already given up. "Try again" invites a duplicate key on the account.
2. **The M3 signon walk could not tell them apart.** `S3-provider-key-step`'s recorded evidence can only quote the sentence the page showed, so a timeout and a rejection are the same string in the proof. C5 run [36225016456](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/omniweb/actions/runs/36225016456) failed at 2026-09-26T06:54:31Z with exactly that.

## The change

* `AddCredentialResult`'s failure variant carries `status?: number` — present when the failure came from onex-api, absent when it came from a local guard.
* `addCredentialFailureMessage(status?)` in `action-logic.ts` is a pure function, so every branch is testable without a session, a network call or a rendered tree.
* `apiErrorStatus(err)` is added beside `isApiStatus` in `lib/api-client.ts`. `isApiStatus` answers "is it exactly this one?", which forces a caller branching across several statuses to ask N times; `ApiError` stays module-private.

## What this does NOT fix

The 504 itself. Its cause is the BYOK store's lazy import — ~78s cold, paid inside the first `POST /v1/tenants/me/inference-credentials` of each `onex-api` process — fixed in **OmniNode-ai/omninode_infra#1699**. This change makes the failure legible when it happens; it does not stop it happening.

Also not fixed here: the walk records `S4-first-dashboard` and `S5-first-key-visible` as PASS in the same run, because `lib/onboarding-gate.ts` fails open on an unresolved key count (`count_unresolved` → allow, documented and deliberate). That is AC3 of OMN-19762 and deliberately left alone while C5 is being driven back to 3/3 — changing what the proof measures mid-flight would make the next three runs uninterpretable.

## Verification

`app/(app)/app/inference-credentials/__tests__/add-credential-failure-omn19762.test.ts`, 6 checks, discovered by `scripts/ci/run-unit-tests.ts`.

The last two are the positive control: a branchless implementation that always returned the generic sentence passes those two and fails the four above them, so the suite cannot be satisfied by "the message changed".

Ran locally: 6 passed. Sibling suites unaffected — `validation.test.ts` 16 passed, `api-client.test.ts` 8 passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Linear: OMN-19762
